utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Judge Van den Wyngaert is unable to sit this morning and we'll proceed under the Rule. There's a procedural matter, we gather. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour. We would kindly ask to go into private session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Your Honours, the Defence complained because the Prosecution did not provide to them a so-called investigator's note describing two conversations with Mr. Baki Halimi during the last part of 2005. It is correct, Your Honours, that until Wednesday the Prosecution did not produce such a note and disclose it to the Defence. The Prosecution did that on Wednesday because it received a communication from Defence counsel indicating that the statement of Prosecution investigator Thomas Kuehnel refers to a meeting with Mr. Baki Halimi. And when I received -- and the Defence asked, Well, is there an investigator note? Can you please give us a record of this meeting. I then spoke with the investigator in this case, and I asked the investigator to produce a note from his notes that he wrote at that meeting. And I will say in all candour, Your Honour, that I was present at one of those meetings with Mr. Halimi in late 2005 and simply, Your Honour, there was an error. No investigator note was produced in late 2005. But the matter doesn't end there, Your Honours. In a signed witness statement by Prosecution investigator Thomas Kuehnel, at paragraph 98 Mr. Kuehnel relates that in a meeting with Mr. Baki Halimi, Mr. Halimi told the Prosecution that he was: "Raising funds for the NLA during 2001." That witness statement was disclosed to the Defence in March of 2006. So the Defence have been in possession of the core point from the conversation with Mr. Halimi, the conversations I should say, for the past 18 months. Therefore, in the Prosecution's submission, with respect to Mr. -- with respect to information provided by Mr. Halimi back in 2005, there has been no disclosure breach under Rule 66(B) or Rule 68. The Defence counsel asked the Prosecution counsel for an investigator note and we provided one. If I can turn now to my colleague Mr. Mettraux's submissions about the liability of the testimony of Mr. Bushi and whether that testimony should be allowed. First of all, I should also tell -- I should say to the Chamber that there was certainly no intent on the part of the Prosecution to lead false evidence. Yesterday in a conversation with Mr. Mettraux I was candid with him when he asked me if I "believed Mr. Baki Halimi," what Mr. Halimi had previously told the Prosecution. Whether Mr. Halimi because Mr. Halimi had informed the Prosecution that during 2001 he provided logistical support to the NLA and I told Mr. Mettraux, yes. Therefore, Your Honour, at the close of this trial, the Prosecution will not rely on Nazim Bushi's evidence provided during direct examination on a particular point and this is at page 5609, line 1 to line 3, where Mr. Bushi said that Baki Halimi was not assisting the NLA in any way. However, Your Honour, the final result should not be to discard the remainder of Mr. Bushi's evidence. Your Honour, if the Prosecution has reason to believe that a witness may not be giving completely truthful or accurate evidence on one point, does that mean that the remainder of the witness's evidence cannot be presented? And in the Prosecution's submission, the practice and the jurisprudence of this Tribunal would answer no. In fact, Your Honours, it is an everyday occurrence at trials before this Tribunal that witnesses provide testimony that may not be fully truthful or accurate and the task is then left to Trial Chambers after hearing all of the evidence, to determine what weight, if any, to give to such evidence. And I would respectively refer the Trial Chamber to the Appeals Chamber's discussion of the effort of Witness AT in the Kordic appeal judgement, paragraphs 244 to 294 of judgement dated 17 December 2004. And that discussion by the Appeals Chamber confirmed decisions made by the Kordic Trial Chamber with respect to the evaluation of a Witness AT in the Kordic trial judgement. So, Your Honour, in the Prosecution's submission, both the practice of this Tribunal and the jurisprudence of this Tribunal would not -- would not support the discarding of Mr. Bushi's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could be permitted to reply very briefly. The complaint identified by Mr. Saxon to the effect that our complaint is one about a failure to disclose material clearly relevant to these proceedings and clearly falling within the terms of Rule 68 is incorrect. Yes, this is one of the issue relevant to this matter, but this is not the nut of the problem. Our concern here, Your Honour, is that the Prosecution has sought to elicit, positively elicit evidence which it knew to be false or should have known to be false. The Prosecution attempt to limit the question to whether or not Mr. Halimi was or wasn't a member of the NLA and what role he plays is not correct. The proofing notes which were given to us by the Prosecution in the past few days have a much broader scope of relevance. The second complaint of the Defence is that the Prosecution is now seeking to rely on evidence that it has failed to investigate properly as mentioned by my colleague Mr. Apostolski. A third complaint is that the Prosecution seeks to rely on the evidence of a man who has shown his willingness not to be truthful with the Prosecutor or with the Chamber. Mr. Saxon has indicated that it is for the Chamber ultimately to decide on the reliability or otherwise of a witness and that is correct. There is, however, an obligation in the Prosecution's own internal rules of 1999, Article 2, which compels them only to elicit evidence which they know to be true or believe can contribute to the finding of the truth. Your Honour, the matter is not one of the Defence ability to cross-examine this witness, in our submission. This witness should never have been brought before this Chamber. Furthermore, and I reiterate the fact that the unreliability we submit of Mr. Bushi in relation, in particular, to Mr. Halimi is revealing of his willingness and readiness to be untruthful about the two matters, the two sole matters which are relevant to his evidence, the presence and role of the NLA in or around Ljuboten on the 12th, and his unwillingness or unwillingness to assist the Trial Chamber in obtaining reliable information about the inner functioning of his organisation, the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I make a 30-second point, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Only because the issue is so significant, Mr. Saxon. Otherwise, if there was a matter, you ought to have dealt with earlier. But yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It is simply to correct a statement that my learned colleague Mr. Apostolski made earlier where Mr. Apostolski said that the investigator note disclosed recently to the Defence indicate that Sulejman Bajrami, one of the named victims in this case, was a member of the NLA. This is not correct. The investigator's notes say that according to Mr. Halimi, Sulejman Bajrami was not a member of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that, Mr. Apostolski, you should have another word.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems I will have to resort to my 30 seconds, Your Honours. I said that the brother of Sulejman was a member of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, the Chamber would like to be made more clear in its understanding of the reasons why there had not been a complete and adequate disclosure as required, in particular by Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: An oversight, Your Honour. I cannot give a better explanation than that. Yesterday, after the investigator note related to Mr. Halimi was produced and disclosed on Wednesday, I then began a review of all other investigator notes in the Prosecution's possession, and identified several more investigator's notes which I thought had been disclosed in early 2006. They had not been and they were disclosed yesterday. One of them at least in particular is relevant to the evidence of Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Had not been for the care, then, of the Defence of Mr. Boskoski, this trial might have reached its conclusion without matters of such materiality being revealed. Is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's possible, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber proposes to adjourn now for a little time. --- Break taken at 9.37 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: An issue of considerable significance has been raised by counsel for the two accused. It appears to the Chamber that if it is considered closely, the primary issue is a failure of the Prosecution to have disclosed material information in its possession, information which could well assist the Defence of each accused in the pursuit of their respective cases. The failure to disclose has now been corrected. The focal significance of the information, which has not been disclosed until this late stage, directly relates to the present witness, who is still in the course of cross-examination. It is therefore the case that the material effect of this information now disclosed is able to be used by both Defences in dealing with the witness and in the pursuit of the balance of their respective cases in the trial. It is also the case that this information may have been of value to the Defence for each accused in dealing with some previous witnesses. If there has been some significant adverse effect, that can be dealt with by an application, most obviously, to recall any witness who is so affected. The Chamber is concerned that there should have been such a significant failure in compliance with the rules of disclosure. It is a matter in which the Chamber accepts that there was no knowing or deliberate withholding of information, and, indeed, that is not suggested by counsel for the Defence. But the Chamber is concerned to ensure that the fairness of the trial is not adversely affected, and it therefore will insist that the Prosecution now undertake a complete and further review of its material to ensure that there is no further failure to disclose what is, quite obviously, information of significance to each Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Counsel, in particular for Mr. Boskoski, did raise some additional matters in his submissions. It does appear to the Chamber that each of those matters are really directed to the weight and reliability which should, in the end, be given and attributed to the evidence in particular of the present witness. Those are matters upon which, in light of all the evidence in the trial and the submissions which will undoubtedly be made about them, can and will be effectively considered by the Chamber in its final evaluation of the case. We would add that there can be no question that a witness's evidence may, in part, be reliable, and, in part, not, and the circumstance that in some part evidence is not reliable or is false does not necessarily preclude that witness being called by the Prosecution, despite the particular obligations on the Prosecution in the case, nor, of course, by the Defence, if it is that they choose to call evidence in the case. We are therefore of the view that despite what has occurred, the fairness of the trial is not so adversely affected as to call for any more drastic action on the part of the Chamber. In particular, we are not of the view that it is appropriate that we should order that this present witness's evidence should cease or that we should direct ourselves to disregard what has been said by the witness to date. In fact, in our view, the fairness which we owe to each accused in their trial is likely to be better served by allowing to the Defence full opportunity to explore all aspects of the witness's evidence with a view to a more full and adequate disclosure of its deficiencies. For these brief reasons, the motion of the Defence will not be granted. The witness should be called.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps to indicate a very short matter. The Defence is obviously ready to continue with the cross-examination and we will. It may be, however, that we will seek the postponement of the rest of the cross-examination at some stage, in particular in relation to the issues material to the documents which have been given to the Defence with a view to perhaps obtain further information from Macedonia. At this stage, Your Honour, we will propose to continue and should the need arise, we would indicate it to the Chamber later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that indication, Mr. Mettraux. The Chamber had understood that from the effect of your submission and proceeded on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But clearly, if either Defence is adversely affected in some significant way by the late disclosure, that is a matter that should be raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I remind you of the affirmation that you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we start with the evidence there is a matter which yesterday we had omitted to do and that was to tender the last document which was shown to the witness. This was Rule 65 ter 1D822, this was a special report of the OSCE dated the 21st of March of 2001 which contains a declaration by all Albanian political parties represented in the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia and which rejected the actions and violence of the so-called NLA. Your Honour, we would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D225, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you recall that on Wednesday when we parted I was asking you questions about the goal and purpose of your organisation. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall stating your belief that your organisation had the support and I think you said moral support of the Albanian community in Macedonia. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you recall that I showed you a declaration signed by all political parties represented in the Republic of Macedonia, which rejected the violence used by your organisation. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you agree with the proposition that the suggestion that you had large support, moral or otherwise, from the Albanian population in Macedonia is incorrect. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I abide by what I said about the moral support, whereas in parliament only two political parties were represented, which does not necessarily mean to say that they were the sole representatives of the Albanian people.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, I will ask the question again. Do you agree with the proposition that in fact and in truth you were not welcomed in the Albanian communities which your group occupied. Do you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with it. It is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree with the proposition that the entire international community, every state, every international organisation, rejected your movement as an illegitimate criminal organisation, a terrorist group and extremist organisation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with that because the NLA was not a terrorist organisation. It was a regular army with its uniform and logo and the internal rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown what is Rule 65 ter 1D827, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But let me put that to you in view of your response first, Mr. Bushi. Isn't the truth that it was the lack of legitimacy and the lack of support from the entire international community that led to you pretend to be an army and give yourself military sounding names and military sounding organisations. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is a document, I apologise again it is a document that is in the English only. It doesn't have a Macedonian or an Albanian translation. But this is a document which comes from the OSCE, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, it is dated the 3rd of May of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I will simply indicate there are a number of redactions made in the text of the document. Those redactions were made by the OSCE prior to disclosure to the Defence. I'll ask the registry to turn to page 3 of this document that will be 1D00-7221.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document that talks about the situation in early May 2001 in and around Vaksince and Slupcane. And I would simply read one paragraph to you from this report. Is says this --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I don't have this document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I should be apologising, Mr. Bushi. The document doesn't exist in Albanian or in Macedonian. I will therefore have to read it out to you. Is says this.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. But please more slowly if you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: "There is it deep concern that given the fact that the inhabitants of the villages under control of the ethnic Albanian armed group east of the Crna Gore are not permitted to leave, a call by the government for them to do so would achieve little. Whilst it is a logical demand to make and in line with what one might expect of any other country in similar circumstances, there is a fear that the military/police action may ensure later this afternoon putting many of the assessed 20.000 inhabitants at risk. It is clear that the ethnic Albanian armed group would claim that all villagers are supporters of their cause. This is it emphatically not the case." Isn't that the case, Mr. Bushi, that in fact and in truth your movement had no support in any part or in very limited part of Macedonian society, whether Albanian or Macedonian?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The NLA had the support of all the Albanians, whereever they lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you also know that in a number of villages, including in Ljuboten, Mr. Bushi, villagers protested your presence or your attempts to infiltrate the villages. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Bushi, telling my colleague and myself on Wednesday that the purpose of your organisation was allegedly to promote the human rights of the Albanian people and to deal with what you perceived to be discriminations in public and official function. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, I'm putting to you that that is just a facade and the real purpose of your organisation was to carve a part of the territory and to keep power and money for the leaders of your moment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not correct. Had we wanted to take over parts of the territory, we would have done so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And I'm also putting to that you to achieve that goal you used violence to undermine Macedonian stability and had recourse to criminal and terroristic means to achieve your goals. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please indicate to me what terrorist acts the NLA has committed? And it is not true what are you putting to me. The NLA engaged in a war because the Albanian people was discriminated as of 1990s onwards, even earlier than that, so I can't ask you to indicate a single crime or a single terrorist act committed by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we will come to the crimes and the alleged discrimination in a moment, Mr. Bushi. But isn't that right that the issues or the goals which you claim to pursue through means of violence, murder, expulsion, torture, sexual violence and others were in fact being properly dealt with in democratic fashion by the elected authorities of Macedonia. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with that. I don't know where you got this information from. It is not at all true, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, will you perhaps agree with that then, Mr. Bushi, had you no intention - and by "you" I mean you and your organisation - to play by the democratic rules, to start a political party and to put your ideas forward with a view to seek the support of the people who you claim supported your movement. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our aim, when the first democratic party for democratic prosperity was form was that after we saw that, the political parties did nothing to redress the demands of the Albanian people, which fell in the deaf ears of the Macedonian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll turn to that right now, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But before I do so, Your Honour, I would seek to tender the document that is on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D226, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would the registry please bring up what is Rule 65 ter 1D713, it has an ERN of 1D00-6274.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, the document that I am about to show you is again, unfortunately, in English only so there is no translation in Macedonian or Albanian, but I will read it out to you. This is the record of a hearing before the committee on foreign relations of the United States of America at the Senate. It concerns the crisis in Macedonia and US engagement in the Balkans. It dated the 13th of June of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I will ask the registry to turn to page 1D00-6278. And if you could please focus on the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, want I want to read to you is simply the last paragraph on that page which is, if you wish, an introduction of the subject matter of this particular hearing of the US Senate, and it says the following: "Today's hearing has a two-part focus. First, we will discuss the extremely volatile situation in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, a country that just one year ago was considered a model of inter-ethnic cooperation but now teeters on the brink of civil war."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask the registry now to turn to page 1D00-6283.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm going read to you is the statement of one high-ranking US Senator, Mr. -- or Senator Helms who expressed his view about the situation in Macedonia in the following terms: "Until recently Macedonia was a model, albeit an imperfect one, for inter-ethnic co-existence and democratic rule in Europe's most war-torn region. Now, within the past few month things have changed. Ethnic Albanian terrorists are today using violence in an effort to undermine Macedonia's stability." Mr. Bushi, do you agree that's what you were doing at that time in 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true. The reality is different from what you read to me, the actual reality was completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Let's go on reading then. Senator Helms says: "Now, I realise that there are legitimate Albanian grievances--" well, I missed a sentence. I will start again: "Indeed, I am impressed by the restraint with which the government of Macedonia has responded to these vicious attacks. Now, I realise that there are legitimate Albanian grievances in Macedonia but none warranting a turn to violence." And he goes on to say this: "This point has been wisely underscored by the refusal of Macedonians leading ethnic Albanian parties to side with the terrorists. Instead, ethnic Albanian parties have condemned violence and are working with other Macedonian political parties as part of a national unity government, and the potential success of this unity government is a threat to all ethnic extremists in the Balkans." Isn't the truth, Mr. Bushi, that you and your organisations made everything in your power using violence, crimes to prevent a unity government to take care of those issues which you say you were trying to promote. Isn't that the truth, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will respond to your question. But, Your Honour, I would kindly ask you to give me more time to go in greater length in my response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Try giving your answer, Mr. Bushi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not true what the counsel is putting to me. You should know that in the Macedonian parliament there was a member who later joined the NLA members precisely because of the discrimination that was perpetrated against Albanians from 1991 because the demands put forward by the Albanians through their political parties were disregarded. I know that the United States, NATO and the international factor does not sit down to negotiate with the terrorists. In 2001 the war was over after an agreement was signed, namely the Ohrid Framework Agreement with guarantees put forward by the United States, NATO, and the European community.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, I'm grateful for this answer and we go to the issue of the parliament in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But at this stage I will ask the registry to turn to page 1D00-6284. And will ask the registry to focus on the second half of the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm about to read to you is a statement made by Ambassador James Pardew, senior advisor on the Balkans, Bureau of European Affairs, Department of State, and it still before the US Senate, but before I do that, do you know who Mr. James Pardew is and was in 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you help the chamber -- [Previous translation continues] ... and can you tell what function --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was one of the mediators between the NLA and the Macedonian forces, especially in the case of the withdrawal from Haracin.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But his real function was not to mediate between you and the government; his real function was to assist the legitimate democratic political parties in Macedonia to reach an agreement which would allow the country to return to a more peaceful existence. Isn't that true, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true, but that was also true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the evaluation which Mr. Pardew gave of the situation in Macedonia in 2001. And I will read it out to. It starts with the word "the situation today." "The situation today in Macedonia is precarious. The insurgence National Liberation Army, NLA, launched its first attacks in north-west Macedonia in February. Since then, the fighting has continued off and on largely in ethnic Albanian areas. Most recently the NLA occupation of the town of Aracinovo near Skopje and its airport poses a potential threat to NATO supply lines." And he goes on to say this: "No one should mistake the position of the United States administration. We absolutely oppose the NLA's use of violence to undermine the democratically elected Macedonian government and its leaders. We condemn the NLA's apparent effort to provoke an overreaction by the government against Albanian citizens in order to bolster their support from the ethnic Albanian community." And that's what I put to you yesterday, Mr. Bushi, or Wednesday - you may recall it - that's what you were trying to achieve in Ljuboten when you ordered your men, the people under you in your organisation, to shell the position of the Macedonian forces in or around Ljuboten. You tried to lure them into the village to create an incident and then to use it for propaganda purposes and to increase the support of your organisation. Isn't that what you did, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not true. I already said that. We didn't need such propaganda because the NLA was an organised army force and we could have infiltrated everywhere we wanted in Macedonia, not only in Ljuboten. From what I see here, James Pardew didn't say anywhere that NLA is a terrorist organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we will come to that in a minute. But at this stage you will recall that I showed a document where NATO officers had expressed the same view, namely that you were trying to provoke incidents involving the Macedonian forces to bolster the support of your organisation. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that document, but it is their own statement. We have quite different strategies and that is why we had the successes we had in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we will put this document aside, the Senate record, and we come back do it in a minute but I'll show you another document in the meantime. That is Rule 65 ter 1D688 and it has an ERN 1D00-6053. Mr. Bushi, this is again a document in English. This one is a report from a renowned military magazine called Jane's Intelligence Digest and it is from the 1st of February of 2001 and there are several parts of this document I would like to read to you. If the registry could go to the second part of the page. Thank you very much. The assessment of this review, Mr. Bushi, about what was going on in Macedonia, in particular and in the Balkans in general was as follows: "Current events in the Balkans indicate that Jane's Intelligence Digest oft-repeated warnings of an escalating series of regional conflicts are proving accurate. In a space of a week ethnic Albanian terrorists have launched an attack on a Macedonian police station, 2.000 Kosovar Albanians have been fighting with KFOR troops in Mitrovica and there has been a serious upsurge in the conflict between the Serbia forces and ethnic Albanians in southern Serbia." Then it goes on to say: "All of these incidents have a common root, radical Albanian nationalism." I will ask the registry to turn to the next page, please, and to focus on paragraph which starts with the words: "The low-level attacks." The magazine goes on to say that: "The low-level attacks against the Macedonian police which began last year are supposedly the work of the so-called liberation army, four of whom have been arrested. Ethnic Albanians make up an estimated 25 to 35 per cent of Macedonia's population of 2 million and are settled predominantly in the west of the country. "The Macedonian Albanians currently have a tense but generally productive relationship with the government in Skopje. Prime minister Ljupco Georgievski's coalition government includes an ethnic Albanian party among its partners. Many observers suggest that the Macedonian Albanian leadership is willing to wait for a generation before pressing their demands for independence. This is because of the Albanian's higher birth rate would provide them with an increasing democratic advantage as this century progresses." And if we can turn to the next page, please. The piece goes on to say: "At present KLA terrorism in Macedonia is still a relatively minor issue just as it was in Kosovo from 1995 to 1998. The KLA started its activities by attacking Serbian police patrols. However, the ultimate aim is to provoke the authority into making a military response which will serve to unite the ethnic Albanian minority in western Macedonia." Mr. Bushi, there again you will agree that this magazine and its authors have also taken the view shared by members of the US Senate that is what you were up to, what you were doing with your activities was to seek to lure the local authorities, in particular the security forces, to respond to your attacks with a view to attract sympathy for your organisation and I will add that did you that in complete disregard for the well-being of the citizens, whether Albanians or Macedonians. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with that, sir. You know that when the Tetovo University was opened by the Albanians with their own funds, the Macedonian police killed a student for the sole reason that he wanted to learn in his own mother tongue as the other Macedonian citizens. What kind of provocation are you talking about, coming from what side? The actual situation in Macedonia and what these newspapers write is quite different. We have facts to prove that. If we want to speak on the basis of facts, let's do that. If we want to speak using statements such as these, we can write -- or you can write such statements every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence seeks to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D227, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'll ask the registry to go back to Rule 65 ter 1D713. That is the Senate record of a hearing on the 13 of June of 2001. And I will ask the registry to turn to page 1D00-6291. If the registry could focus on the second half of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm going read another passage, Mr. Bushi, of this record of the Senate of the US Senate about the situation in Macedonia and there is a question which is being asked of Ambassador Pardew by the chairman of the committee, which is senator called Joseph Biden, and he asked this: "Let me begin, Mr. Ambassador, by asking you about something you directly -- you indirectly referenced but I would like to be more direct. What do you think is the proximate cause of the violence in Macedonia now?" And if one looks down further down in the text is the answer of Ambassador Pardew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, but the accused are not receiving interpretation in the Macedonian language. Now it is all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful again for the indication to Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, I'll read to you the answer that Ambassador Pardew gave to the question of chairman Biden about what was the proximate cause of the violence in Macedonia and he said this: "Senator, first of all let me start with the situation back before February. The Macedonian government was in a dialogue with its Albanian minority community which is substantial. The estimates range from 25 per cent to 35 per cent of the population is ethnic Albanian. They were in a dialogue. They had brought them into the government in many areas, but that dialogue continued because their record in dealing with the rights of their minority citizen was not perfect. "Beginning in February while most of everyone's attention was focussed on southern Serbia and the insurgency that was ongoing there, a group of extremists - exactly whether they were Macedonia originated in Kosovo is not quite clear - began to form and to take military action against the government forces in north-west Macedonia." Mr. Bushi, you will agree that when you and your colleague took up arms against the state purportedly to defend certain rights or human rights of people you claim to represent, those very issues were in fact being dealt with by the democratically elected authorities. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not, because these issues were not treated in a democratic way. Had that happened in reality the war of 2001 would not have happened. As I said earlier, the Macedonian political class imposed this war on us. At that time we were represented by 25 to 35 per cent, as it is said in the document, I wouldn't have said maybe 35 per cent, as I pointed earlier, until 2001 in the police forces --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the percentage of the Albanian representation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And can you tell me now out of this percentage in representation of Albanians, where do you see this equality and what representation do you have in mind? Can you point a concrete case of a fair representation of the Albanians which would be 15 per cent, 16 or 70 [as interpreted] per cent. Menduh Thaci started to negotiate with his partner Ljupco Georgievski and they had no political agendas during their mandate. They only had their private business agendas and time will prove this true. There was a demand for an Albanian university at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, you asked for percentages and I will give you some in a minute but at this stage you indicated that because they were not treated in that democratic way, are you suggesting that the election by free citizen of representatives of the political party which they choose of the ethnicity of the party which they choose and the involvement of ethnic Albanian ministers and parties in the government is not a democratic route. Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I will tell you why I'm saying this. The Albanian democratic party did not win the election at that time. The PPD won the elections. However, Ljupco Georgievski took for his partner Menduh Thaci. The same thing happened on the year of 2006 on the 5th of July when the BDI won the majority of votes, the democracy says that the people should decide on who will represent them in the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi -- [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but I did not finish. Let me finish with my answer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, is your evidence that what you did --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you allow me to finish my answer, sir. I only have two or three more words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your answer, please finish, Mr. Bushi, but it is a very long answer and you're ranging well beyond the question, but please give your answer on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will try to be as short as possible and within the context. The same thing is happening nowadays. The PPD is in coalition with the VMRO-DPMNE and I don't know how well-informed you are with the current political situation in Macedonia. I thank you and sorry for taking so much time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And just one last question before the break. From your response, Mr. Bushi, on the stand what you didn't like in the democratic party is that the representatives or the people who represented the interests of the Albanian people in parliament and governments were not to your liking, not of the people of Albanian ethnicity in Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not what we will choose but those who will be chosen by the people should represent their people, not those who are chosen by individuals.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, page 34, line 2: PPD should be replaced with PDSH.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure whether you would wish to take the break at this stage or in view of the procedural matters, you prefer to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is necessary I think to have the break now, Mr. Mettraux, and we resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, there are two more passages of the record of the Senate, the US Senate which I would like to bring to your attention. The first one is at page 1D00-6295.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if I could request the registry to go to the middle of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I will read out to you is a further assessment by Ambassador Pardew, the US envoy to Macedonia in 2001, about what was going on in the country and in particular what the Macedonian government at the time was trying to do. And it says this: "The Macedonian government was working in an open -- in an ongoing dialogue with the Albanian community at the time this fighting broke out. That process was not moving rapidly enough in either our view or in the view of the Albanian community. I think this conflict has heightened the awareness of the government that they do need to take actions here. There are any numbers of inequities in terms of Albanian participation in the institution of government, the police force, the military, their access to resource, their cultural identity, language and so forth. Those issues are on the table in the discussions that are going on now with the legitimate and accepted political parties that the Macedonian government has been dealing with all along." Isn't that the truth, Mr. Bushi, that at the time when you took up arm under the pretense of defending or promoting the human rights of the Albanian community in Macedonia, those issues were dealt with by the government perhaps not rapidly enough but all of them were on the table being dealt with democratically. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that, because of the following: Had these demands been on the table of discussions between the Macedonian and Albanian parties, Isli -- Isni Thaci, the member of the Albanian democratic party, would not have left the parliament but instead he did and he joined the ranks of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this, then. Isn't the truth that you were not willing to wait for the democratic process to follow its course but what you really wanted was power for yourself and your organisation. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. We no longer trusted the Macedonian institutions since from 1991 there was no progress in the issue of the Albanians being treated equally with the Macedonians.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let me read to you another statement of Mr. Pardew what he says about the goals, the true goals and purposes of your organisation. That's the previous page of that document. That's 1D00-6292. Mr. Bushi, Ambassador Pardew was asked by a senator about the goals and purpose of your organisation and that is what he said: "Senator, at its most basic level, I think the objectives of these people who are running this insurgency are personal power for themselves and they are pretty flexible on what they would accept. I think some of them would like to see this romantic notion of a greater Albania but that is probably a very small element. I think some of them would like to partition Macedonia, but at the end of the day I think they are seeking greater political influence inside the Albanian community both in Macedonia and in Kosovo." Mr. Bushi, isn't that the truth what your organisation is all about is to get power for yourself through the use of violence. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is not true. I don't agree with that. And when you speak about division of Macedonia, sir, the prime minister at that time Ljupco Georgievski, came up with a proposal for division of Macedonia and our political representative Ali Ahmeti did not agree with that proposal and Ljupco Georgievski is coming up with a similar proposal even nowadays.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's stick with the goals and purposes of your organisation for the moment. You will recall that you told my colleague that what you were allegedly seeking through the activities of your organisation was greater representation of the Albanian minority in public and official positions. Do you recall telling me that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Sir, in the year 2001, can you tell this Chamber how many Albanian ministers were in the government at that time?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say four. But representation should not be looked as -- to the level of the assembly. There was no similar representation in the institutions. If you're familiar with the process of the formation of the government in Macedonia, you should know that this is an agreement between the members of the parliament discussing certain issues on the table. What is important is the representation in institutions. Even in those ministries which were headed by Albanian there were no Albanian employees.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's take one institution at the time. I was not talking about the parliament at this stage, Mr. Bushi, but in fact there were not four, there were five Albanian ministers in the government at the time. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the government of Macedonia at the time was made of 14, 1-4, ministers. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact number but it should be more or less that figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: You would agree that there was more than a third of ministers of Albanian ethnicity at that time. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, as I said, you cannot speak of a representation of Albanians only through five ministers in the government. Within Macedonia there are many institutions and at that time the representation in this institutions was 1 to 2 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's stick with the government for a bit longer. Do you know how many deputy ministers were of Albanian ethnicity at that time?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say four or five or three. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, there were four. And, again, four out of 14. So that is a bit less than a third this time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And one of them was the deputy minister of the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's Mr. Refet Elmazi. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Who nowadays beats MPs in the Macedonian assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree Mr. Bushi, that as far as the government of Macedonia is concerned and as far as the year 2001 is concerned, there was adequate representation of the ethnic Albanian minority in the government. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't agree. There are 700.000 or 800.000 Albanians in Macedonia and you cannot speak of a fair representation of Albanians by a number of five or six deputies. If you speak of a proportionate representation which will be in line with the number of the -- percentage of the population, 25 or 26, then I would agree. If we speak about the Ministry of Defence, for example, when there are 8.000 or 9.000 officers, when -- or 10.000, 12.000 officers, and if you compare it to 80 or 90 officers, then you in percentages would be 1 or 2 per cent. That's why I'm saying cannot speak of fair representation of the Albanians from 2001 we still haven't reached the just representation but there has been a progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, can you answer my question about the government. Would you agree that the representation of the ethnic minority, Albanian ethnic minority was in line or in fact perhaps even superior to the democratic percentage -- demographic, I should say, percentage of the Albanian community in Macedonia. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that and I don't know which formula you're using to come up with these figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I should ask you this, Mr. Bushi: How many ministers or what percentage of ministers or MPs or other public offices would satisfy your organisation that is there a fair representation of the ethnic Albanian community? What percentage is acceptable to your organisation?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For us, I'm not speaking now about MPs. This should be based on the vote of the people. It with be 3, 10, 20, 30, depends on the turnout of the population in the voting. But for ministers, for example, this is again an agreement between the governmental parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not finish. And I please ask you to let me finish my answer. You asked me about the ministries. For us it is not important. You can have one minister in the government. For us it is important to have an equal representation in the Macedonian institution, for example, to have Albanians employed in the public administration, in the army, in the police, in the judicial system and other ministries. So we are all seeking just a representation that we rightfully deserve, according to the statistics of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Bushi, I agree with you. There was a democratic process in place at that time in Macedonia, and in fact the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia have made use of that democratic process by voting for certain parties to represent their interests in the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia. And I'm going ask you this: Do you know how many ethnic Albanians were members of the parliament of the republic in the year 2001. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that's absolutely correct, Mr. Bushi. There were two Albanian parties, which made together 21 ethnic Albanians and four ethnic Albanian independent. And can you tell perhaps this Chamber as well how many members there were in the parliament in the year of 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to make a correction. 21 were Albanians. There are two political parties and no independent candidates. 14 members came from the party for democratic prosperity while the 11 others came from the party -- democratic party of the Albanians while the Macedonian assembly numbered 120 MPs at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's right. There were 120 MPs at the time and there were 25 ethnic Albanian in the parliament at that time. You would agree that it is slightly superior to about 20 per cent of the voting population. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the number of MPs yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you agree, Mr. Bushi, that the ethnic Albanian community at the time was able to vote for the party which they thought best represented their interests and they so did. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And would you also agree with that, Mr. Bushi, that today in parliament there is still the same number approximately of representatives of the Albanian community and there is only one slight difference in the representation of this community is that you and your party have now grabbed a bit of power by getting a number of your men in parliament. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only difference here is that we won the parliamentary election of 5th July, 2006 with 11 deputies, while the party which is the ruling party with the VRMO-DPMNE has 18 members. What is going on with Macedonia is totally different from the situation in 2006 and 2007. As a result of the government coalition, the [indiscernible], BDI Macedonia won the candidate status country for integration in the EU and NATO structures, but now Gruevski liked Menduh Thaci as an individual and what they are doing is creating a political crisis in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's put that in simple terms, Mr. Bushi. Do you agree today there is the same number of ethnic Albanian ministers in government as there was in 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of ministers is the same but the employees in institutions, this number differs. In the Ministry of Interior today you have 17 or 18 per cent. In the army, again, the same percentage. In other institutions as well, in the judicial system, in the courts. So the number has reached a difference from 2001. But the number cannot be the same now with the one compared to five years ago. As I said earlier, you cannot look at the representation with a number of ministers in the ministry. You should look at this with the number of representations in the institutions. The number of deputies MPs in the parliament, on this number it is the population who decides, not Ali Ahmeti or Gruevski. It's the population who chooses the number of MPs that will represent them.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And isn't the case, Mr. Bushi, that when you say that the current government is creating a political crisis in Macedonia, you are doing nothing else than what the leader of your political party, the former leader of your organisation Mr. Ahmeti said in parliament a few months ago is that he would bring back 2001 if you and your party didn't get your way, and by that he meant a big sharing of power with his political party. Is that what you're telling?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters kindly ask the witness to slow down.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not Ali Ahmeti who wants this. It is the population that decided on this. They voted on the 5th of July and they entrusted the BDI to represent the demands of the Albanian before the Macedonian assembly. Today the BDI has 15 mayors starting from Struga up to Kumanovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So we can agree on one thing, Mr. Bushi, is that what you care about is the interest of your political party and your organisation, not the interest of the Albanian people. Do we agree on that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true, sir. As I said earlier, people voted on 5th of July and they trusted their vote to Ali Ahmeti and the BDI won the majority of the votes to represent the Albanians in the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Didn't the BDI, sir, get 13 seats in the parliament, which is about 10 per cent of the voting population. Isn't that what happened?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the case. The 5th of July election resulted in BDI having 18 members, PDSH 11 members.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And several of the elected member of your political party later left your party, disgruntled by your politics, is that right, so now you're down to 13 seats. Isn't that correct, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct that we have 13. We have 16 members, sir, but this happens in the parliament of Macedonia because someone is offered means, opportunities, business opportunities and for this reason they vote some, but the majority of the Albanian population gave the vote to the BDI on the 5th of July, and that's a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well you've also mentioned the mayors and claim to have 13 mayors within your ranks. Do you know how many ethnic Albanian mayors there was in --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said 15. I didn't say 13. I said 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Going back to the year of 2001 when you and your group took on the states through violence for the alleged purpose of promoting the position of the Albanian ethnic community in Macedonia, do you know how many ethnic Albanians were mayors in the country at the time?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the accurate number, but there were mayors of some villages with the exception of Tetov and Gostivar. I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, would 26 out of 123 be about right, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be true, but in 2004 the electoral code was abandoned. So if there were 123 communes at that time, now the number is about 70 or 80. I'm not sure. There is a change, actually, that with the amendment made to the self-governing authorities, the borders, the borders of the municipalities have changed. So in Skopje we have Izmet Mexheti, the chairman of the commune of Cair, that of Strumerko [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The point that I'm taking to is slightly different. I don't think we need to go into the detail of local laws at this stage. But what I'm putting to you is that in 2001 when you took up arms allegedly to help the ethnic minority get a greater representation in the state, there were more than 20 per cent of the mayors which is another elected position in Macedonia which were held by members of that community which corresponds, more or less, to the demographics of the country. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We are talking of commune chairmen but not all their rights and powers that they had in 2001 and the amendment of the electoral and the local governing which, after the Ohrid Framework Agreement had -- were given greater powers in the context of the decentralisation of central power and to the local power. We cannot talk of the rights of the chairmen of communes rights which they had from 2001 onwards because the change is major in the sphere of the powers and competencies of the commune chairmen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I move on to another document I seek to tender Rule 65 ter 1D713. This is the record of the hearing before the committee on foreign relation of the United States of America. It is dated 13 of June, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D228, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't the truth this, Mr. Bushi, is that you and your organisation were never willing or ready to play the democratic game and you bullied every person, Albanian or Macedonian, who dared to disagree with your agenda. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not true, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown 1D158, please. It is N005-7408 for the Macedonian translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm about to show you is a document which I think you have on your screen in the Macedonian language. This is a summary of security related intelligence. This was gathered by the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia and more specifically by the administration for security and counter-intelligence, the UBK, and it is dated the 19th of March of 2001. I'd like to draw your attention to the second paragraph in that document. I will read it out to you. It says this: "We were informed that the leaders of the newly established NDPA party of Kastriot Hajisheksa [phoen] are exerting tremendous pressure in the parliament upon Arben Xhaferi and the followers of the DPA to withdraw from the government. Similar pressure is also being exerted by the Albanian emigrees in western Europe and the USA. Their aim to provoke a political crisis in Macedonian." And further down in the text the UBK says the following: "The services source from the BPA informed us that the BPA leadership is being pressured to withdraw from the government." Is that correct, Mr. Bushi, that you and your colleagues from the NLA were putting pressure, including physical threats, upon the democratically elected of the Albanian community for them to leave the government and thus create a crisis in the country. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with that, sir. Show me one example of a member being beaten or killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll show you another example, Mr. Bushi. Is that correct that in May of 2001 a grand coalition of political parties which included all major political parties including two Albanian political parties formed a new coalition government. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, extended coalition. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the purpose of that grand coalition, Mr. Bushi, was to try to deal with the issues which you claimed justified your violence and your insurgency. Is that correct that was the goal of this coalition?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the goal of that coalition was. I just know that it was extended or a grand coalition.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But what you will know for certain, Mr. Bushi, is that you and your colleagues did not stop attacking security forces or cleansing villages and areas from citizens. You continued with your activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we continued with our activities, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And your activities, Mr. Bushi, were essentially to provoke the Macedonian forces, kill and maim civilians and representative of the authorities and members of the security forces. Those were your activities. Is that right, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our activities were dealing directly with the Macedonian police and army forces but not against the civilians. We have a fact during the war in Karadak area, we had hostage taken by the Macedonian army and the civilian before the Ohrid Framework Agreement was signed, they were released to go home, and we had our rules and I mentioned that earlier on the first day of my testimony here. At the centre for training, when we clearly indicated to the soldiers that no hostage, either military or civilian, could be killed. And that nobody should shoot at the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we will come to your rules and compliance therewith. But isn't the truth, Mr. Bushi, that the way in which your organisation was promoting, you say, the human rights and position of the Albanian minority in Macedonia at the time was by blowing up convoys of army, shooting and executing members of the security forces. That's how you advanced your agenda. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that the witness be shown Rule 65 ter 1D712. It has been shown already on Wednesday and I will ask the registry to go to page 1D00-6272.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm about to show you is the same document prepared by the human rights organisation the Balkan human rights which is associated with the Helsinki committee and there's a number of matter of relevance to this case which they highlight in this report. And I would like to bring to your attention one particular part of this report or collection of information and it relates to the NLA against new government in Macedonia. And I will read that out to you. There is no Macedonian. "The Albanian guerillas of the National Liberation Army, NLA, in Macedonia said Tuesday that the new government of national unity would only continue the bloodshed and destructions and that negotiation with the NLA are the only hope to end the crisis in the country." I'll stop there for a minute, Mr. Bushi. Isn't the truth that all you were interested in again was to be involved yourself, not the Albanian community, but yourself and your colleague into that process and that you did not give the Macedonian government a chance to achieve any of the goals which you say you were pursuing. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not agree with that. It is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's a comment which is attributed to one of your colleague, another so-called brigade commander, Mr. Sokoli and he says this: "Any kind of government that it is created with the cooperation between the EU without the inclusion of the NLA would only continue the bloodshed causing even more damage." Isn't this, Mr. Bushi, a direct threat from your colleague Mr. Sokoli that they would not stop until that time when you would become part of the matter? Is that what he's telling here?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. At that time we did demanded to have contacts with the political parties for them to uphold or demands, until the Ohrid Agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Sokoli goes on to say this: "According to Sokoli it is not time for governments of unity but it is time for Macedonian authorities and NLA to sit at the table and negotiate. If it has come to this crisis, then the initiators of the crisis should sit down, the Macedonian party on one side, that is shelling the Albanian villages and the Albanian party on the other side that are protecting the villages, Sokoli said." But what Sokoli said, with respect, Mr. Bushi, is nonsense because that is precisely what was happening at the time, wasn't it? All democratically represented political parties, Albanian and Macedonian, were sitting at the same table to try to improve the situation of the minority in Macedonia. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking now about the Ohrid Agreement, sir, the talks which led to that agreement?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: No, Mr. Bushi. I'm talking about the new government that was set up in May of 2001 with a grand coalition including the two Macedonian Albanian political party represented in parliament at the time.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But for us, it was unacceptable until we realise our goals, the amending of the preamble in the constitution and the realisation of the demands put forward by the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And Commander Sokoli goes on to say that: "Commander Sokoli harshly criticised two Albanian parties with influence in Macedonia, meaning the democratic party of Albanians DPA and the party for democratic prosperity PDP. According to Sokoli after the recent crisis in the Kumanovo region, these parties do not represent the Albanian population in Macedonia anymore." And he says this: "It is not possible that a political party such as the PPD or the DPA fails to raise its voice against the shelling to continue representing the interests of the Albanian population." But, in fact, Mr. Bushi, what was happening at that time is that you were bringing that onto the people who you claim you were represented [sic]. When new government was set up in May of 2001, you refused to play the democratic game and lay down arms. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th of February, there were no political parties until the 26th of September until the Ohrid Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Bushi, weren't there --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... democratic games were being played.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- two political parties represented in the parliament all through the year of 2001 and from May the 12th or the 14th of 2001, those two political parties were also represented in the government. Isn't that the case, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the government, but they were no longer our representatives because by that time we had our own institutions, the General Staff, the brigades, our political representative.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you are talking about "our representative," you are talking about the representative of your terrorist organisation? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't call him terrorist but the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, that's what you call it to give it legitimacy, Mr. Bushi, but isn't the truth that the word at large - and by that I mean every state in this world and every international organisation - called you by two names. One was a terrorist organisation made of terrorists and the other one was an extremist organisation made of criminals. Is that how you were described at the time, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true. I said earlier, I know that United Nations, the United States of America, NATO and others do not sit down to talk with terrorists. On this occasion they did sit down with us and discuss with all the open questions and we reached the Ohrid Framework Agreement. They became as a guarantor to this agreement, both NATO, the EU. We were a regular legitimate army for the Albanians with our uniforms and logo. We didn't commit any terrorist or criminal act.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you, Mr. Bushi, is that in fact you fooled no one, that the international community at all time in 2001 did regard you as a terrorist organisation or an extremist organisation and actually never sat with you to negotiate the Ohrid Agreement. The Ohrid Agreement was signed between all political party in the country at the time and the international community and the Macedonian authorities refused to sit with an organisation they considered to be criminal. Isn't that the case, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the case. Everyday international representatives came to Ali Ahmeti to discuss the issue of the Ohrid Framework Agreement. It was not reached by the political parties but by the NLA which was presented then by the political parties that were involved in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to the Ohrid Agreement and your alleged involvement therein at a later stage. But at this stage I'll ask that registry show Mr. Bushi Exhibit 45, Exhibit P45. Your Honour, this is the so-called "White Book" prepared by the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia and it has been tendered by the Office of the Prosecutor and I would ask the registry to turn to page N005-7606-0171, and in the Macedonian this would be page N001-5212. Mr. Bushi, I will ask you to focus your attention on a part of the page which has a subheading saying: "Terrorists must be defeated."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document the "White Book" contains a number of statements made by various political figures, including ambassadors, presidents and so on and they are reprinted in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'd like to read to you is a statement made by Mr. Mark Dickenson who, at the time, was Great Britain's ambassador in Macedonia. This is what he said: "The terrorists do not take the advice of reasonable people because they themselves are not reasonable. It seems to me that what they really want is not what they say they want. In their communiques, one time they say they want a federalisation of the country; the other, they demand the status of a constituent nation. And the next time they would most probably demand that the Macedonian constitution must guarantee them the grand prize of the national lottery each week." Isn't that true, Mr. Bushi, that all through the crisis in 2001 your organisation just kept on changing its alleged purposes with a view to attract support that you never had. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D320, please. That would not be the correct document. That would be Rule 65 ter 1D320 and the ERN would be 1D00 dash -- I'm grateful. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, what I'm going to show you is a statement of Mr. Peter Matthiesen, who you will recall was the military attache of the German embassy in Macedonia at the time. The Macedonian version of this statement is at 1D00-2966. And I ask the registry please to turn to page 18 of this statement. This would be paragraph 85, please. Mr. Bushi, Mr. Matthiesen was asked to give his view as military attache for the German embassy at the time of the goals and purpose of your organisation and that is what he told the Prosecution: "The stated objective of the NLA was the demand for more political rights for the Albanian minority. However, according to my assessment, the NLA were fighting for greater Albania. In this context, the travel by Mr. Ali Ahmeti to Kosovo just before the signing of the Ohrid accord must be viewed." Do you agree with that, Mr. Bushi, that in fact what you were aiming at was not more political right for the Albanian minority; what you were trying to achieve is to carve a bit of the territory out of Macedonia. That's what your grand goal was. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was not our goal. As I said earlier, this was the goal of Mr. Georgievski to divide Macedonia at the time but we as NLA did not accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps you will tell me what symbol appears on the flag of your organisation, the so-called NLA, and also on the patches worn by your so-called soldiers. Can you tell this Chamber that appears on this flag and patches?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the uniform, we had the patch that all the Albanians have in the entire world. It's the eagle and the inscription, National Liberation Army, and Albanians they have one flag wherever they are in Montenegro, in Albania, in Macedonia in Kosovo, in Purisevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bushi, that is the symbol as you indicated of the Albanian nation. . You were not fighting under the flag or with the patches of the Macedonian nation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
