utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P45, please. This time it would be at page N005-7606-0167. The Macedonian version would be N001-5208.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Bushi, I should put this proposition to you: Would you agree that your actions in the year --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't have the Macedonian version before me.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise. The Macedonian version would be at N001-5208. Mr. Bushi, would you agree that your actions and the actions of your organisation in the year of 2001 rather than promoting the rights and interests of the Albanian community in Macedonia, your action in fact undermined the rights of the people you claim to represent. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll read to you what the President of the United States of America, President George Bush, said on the 21st of March 2001 about this. He said this: "A small group of extremists determined to destabilize the democratic multi-ethnic government of Macedonia," that's how he described you. Then goes on to say: "The United States and its allies have a long standed commitment to the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Macedonia." Then he adds: "The insurgents in Macedonia claim to be advancing the cause of the Albanian minority. They are not. In fact their violent methods are hurting the long-term interests of ethnic Albanians in Macedonia, Kosovo and throughout the region. We support instead those political leaders in Macedonia and the region who have rejected violence and terror in favour of democracy and dialogue as a way to achieve political change." Do you agree that this is in a few sentences this encapsulates the position of the international community at the time, Mr. Bushi, that your group of men were men of violence who did not want to play the democratic game and who did not represent the best interests of the Albanian community. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the final position of the international factor and that is that they were the guarantor of the Ohrid Agreement. That was signed by the political parties but proposed by Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you also know, Mr. Bushi, that all through the year of 2001 the international community in its entirety continued to view your organisation as a criminal organisation bent on destabilizing a democratic state. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't, because of the fact that I had a meeting with a British captain in Nagustak village. To my knowledge, he was a member of NATO forces, of representatives of the US and Great Britain, and they do not speak with terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's look at Rule 65 ter 1D286. It has an ERN 1D00-2826. Mr. Bushi, again I apologise, this is in the English language only. This is a joint statement by President George W. Bush of the United States and Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder of Germany on the occasion of a trans-atlantic vision for the 21st century. It is dated the 29th of March of 2001. I would like to draw your attention on to one particular statement with those two gentlemen made in that statement. They said this: "Both our countries have long-standing commitments to the territorial integrity of Macedonia. We strongly condemn the violence perpetrated by a small group of extremists trying to destabilise that country's democracy multi-ethnic government. Their violent methods are hurting the long-term interests of the ethnic Albanians in Macedonia, Kosovo and throughout the region. You would agree, Mr. Bushi, that again what President Bush and Chancellor Schroeder were saying is the same. They regarded you, the world regarded you as extremists, terrorists, criminals that would not play the democratic game and that did not serve the interests of your alleged supporters. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I will repeat. We were not terrorists or criminals. These could be in the beginning of the war when Mr. Thaci and his coalition partners, the former Prime Minister Ljupco Georgievski called us terrorists, but as time went by the entire policy changed and it ended up in signing of the Ohrid Agreement. I will repeat again: Had we been terrorists, the US would never sit and negotiate with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll see what the US is calling you then. If the witness could be shown Rule 65 ter 1D233 and I would ask the registry to go to page 1D00-2542? Mr. Bushi, this document is a document that was prepared by the public prosecution of the Republic of Macedonia. It is dated the 20th of November of 2001. And it contains again compilation of certain statements made by a number of political figures in relation to the events in Macedonia at the time. This one is from Mr. Colin Powell of the United States and it is dated not from the beginning of the crisis, as you said, but from the 13th of April of 2001. And this is what Mr. Powell said: "The international community and the United States of America are deeply concerned about the terrorist acts in Macedonia and south Serbia." And then further down he says: "Extremist groups are damaging the long-term interests of the ethnic Albanians in Macedonia and in Kosovo and in the whole region." And that again was the position of not only the US but of the entire international community at the time, wasn't it? They considered you, in the alternative, terrorists or extremists that used terrorist or criminal means to achieve their goals. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. The Macedonian government at that time portrayed us in this picture before the world. I will repeat again. If you have a fact or an example of a terrorist or criminal act carried out by us, please let me know which one it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to those, Mr. Bushi, you can be concern of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But at this stage I will ask that the registry should bring up Rule 65 ter 1D852. It is 1D00-7473, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is again in English only. This is a review -- a news review prepared by the United Nations interim administration mission in Kosovo, also known as UNMIK. And it is dated from the 9th of April of 2001. There is no Macedonian or Albanian translation. Mr. Bushi, it should appear in a second on your screen and when it does I'd ask the registry to go to the second page of the document, which would be 1D00-7474. First I'd like to tried a statement attributed to Mr. Alexander Prosko [phoen], the United States ambassador to the North Atlantic Council. He said this: "Mr. Prosko spoke bluntly to the interim administration council members. No parallel existed between the experience of the Albanians in Kosovo over the past decade and those undergone in the FYROM, the Republic of Macedonia." It goes on: "Donors would pose the question, why spend money on people who refuse to play by democratic rules," he said, speaking directly to the IAC Kosovar Albanian members, Prosko hammered home his point. The choice is yours, don't blow it." And then there's a passage about what Lord Robertson, then the Secretary-General of NATO said in the same form. He said this: "Lord Robertson agreed that the situation for minority Albanians in FYROM was a million miles away from Milosevic's Kosovo. NATO intervened to save Kosovo and its people to build democracy and a multi-ethnic society, Robertson emphasised." And then there's a quote attributed to Mr. Robertson and he says this: "We will continue to fight on exactly the same basis when a small country is put under threat by a bunch of armed gangsters." And then he likened your organisation, the NLA and its fighters, to Milosevic's thugs. Then Lord Robertson emphasised that the Kosovar leadership needed to demonstrate its bellwether attributes by ensuring the men of violence were marginalised and banished from the political process. Mr. Bushi wasn't that a fair summary of what the position of the international community was at the time, that they considered you as what Mr. Robertson once said, "a bunch of murderous thugs?"

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of what we were called, I will repeat again, we were a regular army. When you speak of a multi- ethnic country, Macedonia did not have such a picture, after the first parliamentary election Macedonians started to call all these institutions Macedonian, Macedonian, TV, Macedonian parliament and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Isn't that the truth, Mr. Bushi, that you the members of the so-called NLA were the only ones to regard yourself as an army. The rest of the world regarded you as murderous thugs. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that all called us so.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, for instance, to say of your cousins, so to say, would you agree that Albania and the Albanian government at the time considered you to be terrorists. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 1D712, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is again the same summary of various reports which have been collected into this document by the Balkan human rights organisation, and I will ask the registry to go to page 1D00-6272. And I will ask the registry, please, to go to the last subheading on this page which starts with the word "Meta." Thank you. I will read the passage to you. There's a subheading saying Meta: "Albania will never favour terrorism or extremism." It says "NATO's chief George Robertson and head of the European committee Romano Prodi, received Albanian's prime minister Ilir Meta in Brielle. Robertson assessed the stand of the Albanian government as moderate in connection with the incidents in Macedonia. The Albanian prime minister ensured NATO's general secretary that the Albanian government would be consistent in its stand that it will serve the interests of Albania and stability in the region. After his meeting with Prodi, Meta said that Albania had never and will never favour terrorism or extremism in any form." And then he said this: "We are doing or maximum to keep our borders with Macedonia under control," Meta said. "We want to promote cooperation with all country in the region and we condemn extremism and extremists who think that they can solve problems using violence." "We also expressed our full respect towards the territorial integrity of Macedonia and the sovereignty of Skopje' government." And then Meta also emphasised that Tirana has requested that the Macedonian government engages in making a concrete improvement of the conditions and rights of the Albanian minority by isolating extremists. And then Meta told the EU yesterday his government would not allow the country to become a base for ethnic Albanian rebels fighting in Macedonia. "From Albanian territory," he said, "There is no help that is going to the terrorists."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you aware of the position of the Albanian government at the time towards your organisation, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this is not an official document issued by the ministry of foreign affairs in Albania or the government of Albania. So I don't accept that. It's not like you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, would you accept the same statement then if it came from an official United Nations government, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comments on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll show you Rule 65 ter 54 then. This is it ERN N000-N019. The Macedonian version would be N000-N019-MF. Mr. Bushi, this is an official document from the United Nations which we received through the Office of the Prosecutor. It is dated the 7 March of 2001 and it is the record of a meeting of the Security Council of the United Nations and it also contains a presidential statement which condemns violence by ethnic Albanian extremists in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia. I would first ask the registry to turn to the second page of that document. That would be N000-N020, please. And I'll just read to you one passage at this stage. It says this: "In the ensuing discussion council members unanimously condemned the violence perpetrated by ethnic Albanian extremists affirmed the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and commended that country's government for the restraint it had shown and for its plans to address the situation." Then I'll ask the registry to turn to page N000-N026, please. You will see, Mr. Bushi, that Albania at that time was in fact represented at the Security Council of the United Nations. And its representative at the time was a person called Agim Nesho. I believe this would be a few further -- a few pages further down the line. That would be N000-N026. Thank you. And if I can ask the registry to focus on the bottom of the page, please. In particular, the last three line, please. Mr. Bushi, I will read to you what the representative of the state of Albania said before the Security Council of the United Nations. He said this: "Albania was deeply concerned by the recent violence in this region. His government had repudiated and renounced the behaviour of the terrorist group. He commended the response of the government of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and was confident it would continue to show proper restraint and wisdom." And then the representative of Albania continues by saying, "Albania supported efforts to solve ethnic Albanians problems in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia by constitutional means. In his view, acts of violence run contrary to the interests of Albanians and of ethnic Albanians political sector in Macedonia." He also said that this: "It deprived all Albanians of the international support and sympathy that they had won during the war in Kosovo." Would you agree then, Mr. Bushi, based on this official document that the position of your neighbour, Albania, was to reject your group as a terrorist group and to reject the methods and means which you had chosen to achieve your alleged goals. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with that. It is not an official document of the Albanian ministry of foreign affairs or government.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can turn back to Rule 65 ter 1D712, please. I'll ask the registry to turn to page 1D00-6273.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Is that correct that this position, Mr. Bushi, the position of the Albanian government at that time that you were a terrorist outfit or an extremist outfit was shared by all other member states of the United Nations in 2001. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, I'll read a statement attributed to President Bush of the United States once again. It says this: "US President George W. Bush supports the efforts of the government of Macedonia to fight the extremists who have brought violence to the region, White House press secretary Ari Fleischer told reporters. At least it shows you that that was the position of the United States, Mr. Bushi, that they considered you to be a terrorist or an extremist group. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know, and maybe it was in the beginning, because the date was 7th of March. In the beginning, it might have been so. But I would want to see a document by the United States prior to the Ohrid Agreement where they called us terrorists or extremists.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm going to show you one then and it is dated the 30th of April of 2001. It is Rule 65 ter 1D818. It's 1D00-7180. Sir, again, there is no translation or interpretation -- translation, I'm sorry, in either Albanian or Macedonian of this document. This is a record, semi-official record, from one of the US government web sites about press briefing by this US State Department, and it is dated, as I mention, the 30th of April of 2001. And as you will see, the representative of the United States State Department was asked a number of questions about the situation in Macedonia at the time. And this particular press briefing dealt, in part, with an incident that took place in the town or village of Velce. Perhaps we go into this document, sir. Do you know what happened a view days before on the 29th of April in 2001 in Velce? Do you know what happened there?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I want to see a document of July/August. The date here is 30th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, one step at a time, sir. We will stay with this one for a minute. But do you know --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you know what happened in Velce on the 28th or of April of 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Velce.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, you asked me before if I could ask you about crimes committed by your organisation. Perhaps you will remember that in Velce on the 28th or 29th of April of 2001 a group of -- or members of your organisation ambushed a military convoy at the time, just like your brigade did at Ljubotenski Bacila, and what they did at the time is to blow up the truck and execute and burn the survivors of this explosion. Do you recall that incident?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you would agree, I hope, that the NLA that did that in Velce. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I have to say: What was done was done by NLA in Velce. But it was in the context of an armed conflict between the NLA and the Macedonian army, and everything that was committed when people were dressed in uniforms, we don't consider it as a terrorist act. The same applies to the Macedonian killing our forces. In the case of the civilian massacre against the civilian population in Ljubanci or in Tetovo, when a father and a son were killed by the Macedonian forces, this is an act of terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So, Mr. Bushi, if I understand you properly, burning or setting alight a person or shooting him at close range is all right if he wears a uniform of the Macedonian security forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not burned. They were fired at, and it is something else what happened there. They were not set fire to.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Were you privy to the autopsy report about that particular incident, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So you don't know whether they were burned or not, are you?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw some photos, but it is not true that they were burned. Maybe they were shelled with nitroglycerin. This is something that causes burns, of course, when you use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I see. Well, let's see what the United States Department -- or the State Department have to say about this. It is at page 1D00-7189. And there's a gentleman called Mr. Reeker who is the spokesman of the State Department, and he said this: "I will just point out for those of you that missed it over the weekend, we did issue a statement on Saturday soundly condemning the attack on Macedonian security forces by armed ethnic Albanian extremists, and that statement obviously still stands. This was an ambush that extremists -- by extremists that resulted in the death of eight Macedonian soldiers. We want to extend our condolences to the families of those eight who were killed and to the entire country of Macedonia." Then he goes on to say this: "We noted or have discussed that there has been a strong condemnation of that barbarious attack by the Macedonian Albanian political leader Arben Xhaferi." And I will stop there for a minute, Mr. Bushi. You have mentioned Mr. Xhaferi several times in your attack against him and his political party. Isn't that the truth, Mr. Bushi, that you didn't like Mr. Xhaferi so much--

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: -- because he, unlike you, was willing to go the democratic way and to deal with those issues which concerned his people in a democratic fashion. Is that why you didn't like Mr. Xhaferi and still don't like Mr. Xhaferi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't like Mr. Xhaferi, not him personally but his political party, because it followed anti-Albanian policy. And it was a businesslike political policy. They discussed tobacco, coffee, alcohol issues, and we have facts that prove that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, just for the record, you'll confirm that Arben Xhaferi was an Albanian, right?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Then Mr. Reeker goes on to say: "We have encouraged other ethnic Albanian leaders to condemn this extremist violence as well." And then he goes on to say this: "As you know, we very much support the necessary steps Macedonia is taking to prevent armed extremists from disrupting inter-ethnic cooperation and dialogue which has been taking place in Macedonia over the last few weeks. I think that it should be said that such violence and terrorist activity greatly arms the interests of ethnic Albanians in Macedonia and throughout the region and those that are perpetrating this type of violence should realise this." Then later on he is asked another question, and he says this: "For a decade now, as an independent country, Macedonia has in many ways been a model for how you can be a multi-ethnic country. That is not to say that there aren't problems there. Just as we and other country face these problems, so does Macedonia. The point to make is that the way to address this is through the political dialogue, and I think what we have seen is that they have taken that seriously."

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then if the registry can turn the page, please, to 1D00-7190. Mr. Reeker continues to this: "The violence that is perpetrated by this extreme extremist groups doesn't perpetuate that at all." He was talking of the interest of the Albanians. "It makes the process more difficult. It inflames passions. It makes the situation for ethnic Albanians in Macedonia and throughout the region more difficult as they pursue that. "So you know very well we have been very supportive of Macedonia taking the necessary steps to prevent the armed extremists from disrupting inter-ethnic cooperation and the process of political dialogue which is under way there. And again, we think that those armed things, those terrorist acts which have occurred a tragedy which occurred again this weekend resulting in the loss of life simply makes the situation more difficult and does little to feed progress. And it makes the interests of ethnic Albanians throughout the region more difficult to look at in a serious light." Stopping for a minute there, would you agree, Mr. Bushi, that at least as far as the US state department was concerned, your activities which you say were legitimate combat activities against the Macedonian forces were regard in a rather different light by the international community? They called it terrorist acts. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree. I don't know what they said at that particular moment. What I know is that the Macedonian police forces know -- knew that there was an army, there was a brigade 112 in that area of Velce and Tetovo and of course the conflict between armed forces cannot be called terrorist. Terrorist acts are those carried out against civilians. I mentioned the example of a father and a son killed on a street in Tetovo. You cannot compare these two cases. In Velce it was an action carried out by the NLA. I don't know what exactly happened. Let's suppose that this took place but this was a conflict between two armed forces, not between an armed force and civilians. And I would repeat myself again: From 1991 to 2001, there was no political dialogue between the political party. The Albanian political parties in the parliament articulated their demands. But I will repeat here again: The war, the 2001 war, was imposed on us by the Macedonian political class. Why they didn't care to represent fairly the Albanians in the institutions or to allow them to use their maternal language before the 2001. How can you call Ali Ahmeti a terrorist when he is accepted by all countries in the world and they do talk to him and negotiate with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We resume at five past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, do you recall that before the break you said that you were an army and that you were engaged in what you called a conflict or a war with the Macedonian authorities. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree that this army and this war that you were involved in with the Macedonian authority existed only in your mind and that of your colleagues and in no one else's mind. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Do you agree that as I showed to you earlier and as you well know, the international community as a whole continued to refer to your actions as terrorist acts, extremist actions or pure and simple criminal acts. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you're saying is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And when you say that your so-called political leader, Mr. Ali Ahmeti, was a significant or at least a relevant political figure at the time, I suppose you know that he was put on a list, a black list in the United States, banned from travelling, asset frozen and that he was regarded as an extremist. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said earlier, it was in the initial stages of the war because this is how the Macedonian police, army and government portrayed us before the international community.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: That is quite wrong, Mr. Bushi. That happened on the 27th of June of 2001. Do you recall?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you talking about? About the black lists?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It's so-called presidential order from George Bush the President of the United States which placed your organisation, the so-called NLA, and a number of its leaders and members on a black list, travel banned and assess restrictions, 27 of June of 2001. Are you acquainted with that document?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of that but for your information, Menduh Thaci is also on the black list despite that he was not a member of the NLA. A Macedonian general Stojanov or Stojanovski's his last name was also on the black list and he was a leader of the Lions.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the European Union also adopted such travel restriction and freezing of assets against the leadership of your so-called NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was at a certain time, but not today. Menduh Thaci continues to remain on the black list of the United States of America.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And other government such as the Swiss government also took measures against members of your organisation, in particular those who were collecting funds in Switzerland and in other places on the basis that those people were a threat to national security. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No I'm not aware of that and such things did not happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Can we go back to Rule 65 ter 1D818, please, and I will ask the registry to turn to page 1D00-7190, please. Mr. Bushi, I'd like to go through the rest of this document with you. This is again the transcript of a press briefing of the United States State Department and I would like to draw your attention to a number of additional comments made by the representative of the State Department Mr. Reeker. In the middle of the page can you see that -- it's 1D00-7190, please. It starts with the word: "There is no place in Macedonia." It would be a bit further down in the page, I believe. Thank you. I'll read to you the remarks made by Mr. Reeker. It says this: "There is no place in Macedonian for armed Albanian extremists perpetrating this kind of terrorist attack. And we have been very firm about that. You will see when we discuss or if you have reviewed already the 'patterns of global terrorism' report that discusses in south-east Europe groups of ethnic Albanians who have conducted armed attacks against government forces in southern Serbia and Macedonia since 1999. We have been quite resolute from here that that violence is counterproductive and simply not the way to go." You will agree, I hope, Mr. Bushi that at least as far as the US State Department is concerned, there was no armed conflict. There was a terrorist organisation or an extremist organisation using terrorist means that was taking on a democratically collected government. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then Mr. Reeker goes on to say: "As I said, they have had to take necessary steps to prevent, try to prevent disruption of the inter-ethnic dialogue and we continue to support them in that." And he is talking about the Macedonian authority. Then he's asked by a journalist as follows: "You keep calling them armed extremist groups. I mean, are you going to -- does it matter that you don't -- you are not calling them terrorist at this point?" Then if we could turn to the next page. It would be 1D00-7191, please. The response of Mr. Reeker was this: "I think you know very well and we can review with you again at this afternoon's briefing the process of determining a designation under our law of terrorists. I did not and the secretary has noted on a number of occasion that this type of terrorist activity carried out by these groups is something that we condemn in the strongest possible terms." Would you agree, sir, that at least in April 30 of 2001 the State Department described your activities, the activities of your group or organisation, he described them as terrorist activity. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I will emphasise again, you are talking about statements all the time. I asked you earlier, give me an example or a fact of a terrorist attack or act in Macedonia during the 2001 conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Would you agree me, sir, that the United States and the United Nations, we will see, were not the only organisations and not the only states that regarded and called your organisation, the so-called National Liberation Army, as a terrorist organisation. Do you agree there were other states and other international organisations that called you those names?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they said, but I will repeat again, the NLA was a regular army and not a terrorist organisation. When you call it a terrorist organisation, I want you to show you some facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, in that case I will show you what is Exhibit 1D17. Mr. Bushi, this is a document entitled Paris declaration of the OSCE parliamentary assembly. It took place between the 6th and 10th of July 2001. Sir, do you know what the OSCE is?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that the OSCE, the OSCE membership consists of most, if not perhaps all, European states. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And during that particular session of their assembly on the 6 to 10 of July of 2001, the OSCE adopted a number of resolutions and I would like to show you one. It is at page 4 of that document, please. Mr. Bushi, I will have to read it out to you again. There is no Macedonian or Albanian translation. But it reads as follows: "And that is the --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which item are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: It would start at paragraph 32, Mr. Bushi. That's towards the end of the page and this is the parliamentary assembly of the OSCE which says this: "It believes conflict in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and southern Serbia has the potential to destabilize the entire region. It opposes ethnic Albanian groups in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, Kosovo, and southern Serbia who have instigated violence this past year, condemns repeated acts of terrorism in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia." Stopping there for a moment, do you agree that the OSCE, as with the United States and others, again, referred to your activity not in terms of an armed conflict in which you and your colleagues were involved but in terms of terrorist acts against a legitimate democracy. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the document, but I do not agree with it, because we didn't carry out any terrorist act. Please, I will repeat again, give me a fact, not to me personally but give this Tribunal a fact of such an act.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say this. That is the parliamentary assembly. It calls upon the legitimate political representative of Macedonians, Albanians and other ethnic groups in the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia to focus on continued political dialogue and not violence to resolve pressing issues and grievances of ethnic minorities. Do you agree that the OSCE was also enticing the authorities, Macedonian, Albanians and other ethnic group, to continue with the political dialogue. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They appealed for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And the parliamentary assembly of the OSCE also felt it had to say this: "It reiterate its full attachment to the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia which must be respected in the interest of all its citizens and for the stability of the region." Mr. Bushi, you will agree that the OSCE felt it had to state this because you and your organisation were attempting to dismember the Republic of Macedonia. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not true. It is not the way you're putting it. We also guarded the territorial integrity.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: But you agree that this is not the perception of the OSCE in any case, as far as you can tell from this declaration.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is their view on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Rule 65 ter 54, please. This is N000-N019.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Mr. Bushi, this is again the same document that I have shown you a bit earlier. It is an official record from the United Nations about a particular meeting that took place on the 7th of March of 2001 at the Security Council of the United Nation. And I would like to take you on a tour of world views about your organisation. And I will start with the first page. It says this: "The Security Council this evening strongly condemned the recent violence by armed ethnic Albanian extremists in the north of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia and in particular the killing of three soldiers for that country -- from that country in the Tanusevci area." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And do you agree that it was the Security Council's view in its totality that you and your colleagues were an ethnic Albanian extremist group using violence. Do you agree with that? That is the way they described you.

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how they described us in the initial stages and this bears a date of March 2001. I will repeat myself again: The Ohrid Agreement was reached and nowhere is it stated that the NLA was a terrorist army. This agreement was signed by both Macedonian and Albanian political parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, before I --

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the supervision of the USA, NATO and EU.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, perhaps simply to clarify this, Mr. Bushi, is that your evidence or in any case your brief that after the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement on the 13th of August of 2001, the world stopped to call you extremists or terrorists. Is that your belief?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then I will go on to read that document to you. It says in the next paragraph -- well, first let me ask you this perhaps. Can you recall the particular incidents in which the Security Council refers, the killing of the three soldiers in the Tanusevci area. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vaguely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, vaguely enough to acknowledge, perhaps, that this is regarded and called by the Security Council not as an act of legitimate warfare, as you would have it, but as evidence of violence by an armed ethnic Albanian extremist. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then it goes on to it says this: "In a presidential statement read by Council president Volodymyr Yelchenko of Ukraine, the council described the events as a threat to the stability and security not only of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia but also of the region." Then in the next paragraph: "The council expressed support for actions taken by the government of the former Yugoslav Republic to address the violence with an appropriate level of restrains and to preserve political stability and foster harmony between all ethnic components of its population." Then I would like to show you in that document what various states -- the way in which various states described your organisation and how they qualified your actions and I'd like to turn to page N000-9021. If you look at the -- first at the top of this document you will see there is the record of a statement made by Srdjan Kerim, then the minister of foreign affairs of the Republic of Macedonia. And he recalled that in the past few weeks unidentified extremist militant groups had occupied the northern border village of Tanusevci from where they had continuously provoked armed incidents resulting in the death of three Macedonian soldiers on 4th March. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you can now look at the bottom of the page, please. This is the position of the United States of America through its representative James Cunningham. He said: "There was little disagreement about the responsible and careful way the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia government will handled the violence in the northern part of the country or about the desire of the council to provide support for future helpful actions. And if we could turn the page, please. Mr. Cunningham continues by saying this: "He asked the foreign minister to inform his government that the council understood the prudence with which it had acted and that it saw the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia as an example of democracy based on the rule of law and inter-ethnic cooperation and that the United Nations would do all it can to ensure its accomplishments were not undermined." You would agree, sir, that the description given by the representative of the US of the situation at the time, as far as democratic nature of society in Macedonia differs quite significantly from the one you have proposed in this setting. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to the next representative at the Security Council. It is Jean-David Levitte of France. And he said this to the council: "The council was meeting at a time when small armed groups were provoking serious incidents in the -- on the Yugoslav-Macedonia border, that destabilisation at the regional level must be strongly condemned.". Then if we turn to the Chinese representative further down on the page, Mr. Shen Guofang, he condemned the actions of the extremists. That's how you described you. If you look at the very bottom of the page, there's a statement attributed to the representative of Singapore Kishore Mahbubani and he said that the entire council condemned the ethnic Albanian extremists, if you turn to the next page. And then if you look further down at the representative of Norway, Mr. Ole Peter Kolby, he said that "Macedonia had legitimate security concerns that must be addressed and its sovereignty and territorial integrity must be protected." He then adds: "Norway condemned all terrorist attacks in the region." He said: "They threatened both internal and regional security. Leaders must isolate extremists and clearly condemn violence." We can turn to the view of the United Kingdom, also a permanent member at the Security Council which said the Council seemed pretty unanimous on both the foreign minister's proposal and the situation. He condemned the recent violence by ethnic Albanian extremists and welcomed the dialogue between the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia, NATO and KFOR on practical steps. I'll stop here for a moment. Do agree that all those dates again described your activities as violence, your group as either terrorists or your action as terrorist in nature and your group either as terrorists or as extremists. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. I don't know what you mean by the term "terrorist" or "terrorism." The way that these statements describe the situation differs completely from the real situation on the ground. Please, sir, present here one single fact to prove your point, namely that NLA was a terrorist organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If you go down the page on this document to the statement by the representative of Tunisia you can read that Tunisia condemned the violent actions by the extremists. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And if you can turn to the next page, please. You will see that the representative of Colombia condemned the threats made by the extremists. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's the representative of Mali who condemned the illegal and violent terrorist actions by the ethnic Albanian. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: The representative of Mauritius condemned the actions of the extremists. Can you see this one?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's the council president, the representative of Ukraine, who says, speaking in his national capacity, strongly condemn attacks on Macedonian soldiers by extremist Albanian forces and deplored the violent death of three of them a few days ago. Do you agree again that in the view of the Ukraine representative, in any case, what you were doing was not legitimate acts of warfare but crimes committed against Macedonian soldiers. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- yes, because they know that Ukrainian soldiers were also in Macedonia. They know very well how many soldiers they lost.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And can you look a bit further where Ukraine also commended the Macedonia government for its measured response to the situation so far and its inclination to seek a political solution. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And then there's the representative of Sweden Pierre Schori, who spoke on behalf of the European Union and the associated countries of Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta and Turkey as well as Iceland and Liechtenstein and if we can turn to the next page, again Mr. Schori, the representative of Sweden, condemned the rising number of incidents in the area including the ethnic Albanian extremist attack on 4 March near the village of Tanusevci which resulted in the death of three soldiers. And if we go down that page there's the statement of Vladimir Sotirov of Bulgaria where he said the action of the armed Albanian extremists, that's the way he referred to your activities. And if we can turn to the next page, please. There's the statement of representative of Yugoslavia who also referred to you as ethnic Albanian terrorism. And if we go further down that page, there's, once again, the statement which I have read to you from the representative of Albania, Mr. Agim Nesho, which referred to you as a terrorist group and made the point that the acts of violence, your acts of violence run contrary to the interests of Albanians and of ethnic Albanians political sector in Macedonia. Can you see that, Mr. Bushi?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: So will you agree, Mr. Bushi, that the international community was absolutely consistent and unanimous in the view it took of the nature of your organisation as an extremist or terrorist organisation that used violence against the Macedonian state. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not, sir. Terrorist acts were committed by the Macedonian police when, in Manastir of Bitola where Albanians were beaten up, their houses were set fire to. A mosque was burned, which to this day is destroyed. That is a terrorist act where the police forces of the Macedonian government killed civilians. Show me one single act committed by the NLA like the ones committed by the Macedonian police forces. In Manastir of Bitola, there wasn't a single NLA soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: And you said earlier in response to one of my question, Mr. Bushi, that you believed that those names that you were called, extremist and terrorist, were just a thing of the early days and that it soon stopped. And I would like to show what you what is Exhibit 1D115, I believe. It has an ERN 1D00-2009. It could possible possibly be 1D15 rather than 115. Thank you. Sir, this is a statement by the president of the Security Council of the United Nations again. It is dated the 13 of August of 2001 and it greets, if you wish, the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement the same day. And in the statement the president says this on behalf of the Security Council. It reiterates its call to all who have contact with extremist groups to make clear to them that they have no support from any quarter in the international community. The council condemns the ongoing violence by extremists and call on all parties to respect the cease-fire. The council rejects any attempt to use violence, including the use of land-mines, to undermine the framework agreement which has been negotiated by the democratic elected political leadership of the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia. Do you agree that on the 13th of August 2001 after the Ohrid Agreement had been signed the Security Council through its president continued to refer to your group as extremists and referring to your ongoing violence by extremists and asking those who had conduct to you to ensure that you would respect the cease-fire. Is that the way you were being described on the 13th of August of 2001?

utterances.speaker: NAZIM BUSHI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I read here, as you say, that they have called us, in the same word. But in fact we were de facto and de jure a regular army and not at all a terrorist army and nobody can convince me of the opposite. You can convince me only if you provide facts. You only resort to statements here. I'm giving you facts, namely that the Macedonian police and army have committed a terrorist act against Albanians in the course of the conflict of 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, that may be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn now. We resume on Monday at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 1st day of October, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.
